CRM for Public Adjusters and PA Firms — CRM For Claims

# A CRM for public adjusters, not a sales pipeline with claims bolted on

Your licence is a dated document in a named state, your first contact with a client produces five specific documents, and your fee is a percentage somebody could be asked to justify. CRM For Claims holds all three as fields with rules on them — the licence expires on the date it says, and the contract packet will not send without one.

## What a public adjuster needs that a contractor CRM does not have

Most software sold to this industry is built around a contractor who wins a job and then does the work. A public adjusting firm has a different shape: the representation itself is the product, the file is opened by a signed contract rather than an accepted estimate, and three of the things that can end a firm — an expired licence, a contract signed at the wrong hour, a fee above what was agreed — are all matters of record rather than matters of effort.

So the parts of this system a PA firm uses most are not the ones a roofer would name. They are the licence block on each user, the Letter of Representation packet, the fee percentage on the claim, and the report that counts contracts by the date they were signed. Everything else — the stages, the folders, the calendar — works the same for everybody.
